subject: Interop performance debrief & A/B test targets
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Reddy <sana@pegasuscloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + proposed A/B test targets from today's call

Hi Sana — thanks for the run-through today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we all align: 

Summary of call:
- You're evaluating Redwood vs your current hyperscaler endpoint for low-latency customer chat (multi-turn, avg prompt ~125 tokens).
- Primary success metrics: p95 latency, p99 tail, sustained tokens/sec during peak windows, and cost per 1M tokens.
- You need a 2–3 day A/B window to evaluate production-like client traffic.

Proposed A/B test plan (draft):
- Two variants: Redwood hosted API (redwood-standard-quant) vs Hyperscaler model with their optimized runtime.
- Test duration: 48 hours of production replay during your Wed/Thu peak (you confirmed Wed 11/4–11/5).
- Traffic profile: 120 reqs/sec peak, median request ~125 tokens, 6-turn average context.
- Targets to validate: p95 < 180 ms for single-turn, p99 < 450 ms; sustained throughput >= 30K tokens/sec per node cluster.
- Collect: full traces, per-token billing estimates, and KV cache hit rates.

Attachments: I attached a starter AB test spreadsheet and a short checklist for the trace points we need. If you can send the initial logs from your last hyperscaler run (sample traces + token counts), we will prep Redwood-side runs to match.

Next steps: 
1) Can you share the hyperscaler trace bundle by EOD tomorrow? (pegasus-initial-logs.zip)
2) Confirm the 48-hour window (Wed 11/4 00:00 - Thu 11/5 23:59 UTC) or propose alternatives.
3) I'll schedule a brief triage with our infra engineer Rafael to review the trace points and sampling settings.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0168

Attachments referenced: redwood-ab-test-plan.xlsx (staging checklist), pegasus-initial-logs.zip (request that Pegasus shares)
From: Sana Reddy <sana@pegasuscloud.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-team@pegasuscloud.com
Date: 2026-11-02T02:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed A/B test targets from today's call

Thanks Dev — good summary. I'm looping in our infra team and attaching the initial logs bundle (pegasus-initial-logs.zip). Notes from our side:

- We can confirm the Wed/Thu window but need Redwood to avoid rolling deploys during that period.
- Current hyperscaler setup: 8xA100-equivalent instances, autoscale threshold at 60% CPU, custom batching at gateway layer.
- Attached trace bundle includes p95/p99 snapshots from last week and per-request token counts.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) For the p99 measurement — are you using end-to-end (client observed) latency including network hop, or server-side service time? We need to ensure apples-to-apples.
2) Can Redwood produce a per-token cost estimate for the two models we're testing, including expected network egress?

We'll await the detailed AB test doc and Rafael's availability.

— Sana
Sana Reddy
Head of Platform Engineering | Pegasus Cloud
sana@pegasuscloud.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Reddy <sana@pegasuscloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed A/B test targets from today's call

Sana — appreciate the logs. Quick answers and concrete plan: 

Answers:
- We'll measure both: (A) server-side service time (time inside Redwood runtime) and (B) client-observed RTT (including first-byte network). We'll provide both per-request and aggregated p50/p95/p99 so you can pick the metric that maps to your SLOs.
- Per-token cost: we'll run a short cost model based on your sample traces and return an estimated $/1M tokens for each variant (including egress assumptions).

Concrete plan we will execute this week: 
1) Our infra will replay your traces against a matched Redwood cluster (same concurrency profile + batching) and collect: server-service-time, client-RTT (synthetic emulation of your network), tokens/sec, and KV cache hit stats.
2) Rafael will own runtime tunables: batch sizes, prefill parallelism, and quant config.
3) We will push a compiled AB report (CSV + short summary) into the Drive link and ping you when ready. Expect first pass within 36 hours of receiving the traces (so EOD 11/3).

I've attached a more granular sheet (redwood-ab-test-plan.xlsx) with column definitions and the exact traces/headers we'll need. Rafael — can you confirm you can run the replay on Tue night and leave the cluster stable Wed/Thu?

Thanks — Dev
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Interop performance debrief & A/B test targets (internal)

Internal planning notes (do not forward):

Goal: make the AB window decisive and defensible to procurement. Key hypotheses to test: 
1) Redwood's KV cache will materially reduce tokens/sec cost for multi-turn sessions (>3 turns). Check delta in cache-hit-rate and per-token latency when cache warm vs cold.
2) Hyperscaler shows better median but worse tail under synthetic spike; validate p99 behavior under short spikes (5–10s).
3) End-to-end cost advantage by at least 20% after accounting for latency-driven user retries and egress.

Test specifics: 
- Target metrics we should aim to show: p95 <= 150 ms, p99 <= 380 ms in server-side service time for Redwood baseline; sustained cluster throughput target >= 35K tokens/sec for the configuration we'll mirror. Those numbers are intentionally aggressive but defensible based on our last lab run.
- Logging: enable full per-request trace sampling at 5% plus aggregated histograms for 1s windows.
- Post-test artifacts: CSV with per-request latencies, tokens, model variant tag; summary slide with two charts (latency CDF, tokens/sec over time) and a small cost model.

Rafael — flag any infra constraints (GPU count, test scheduling). If we cannot hit those throughput numbers with the planned instance types, we'll propose an alternate, cost-normalized baseline.

Marissa
Sr. Account Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Reddy <sana@pegasuscloud.com>

Date: 2026-11-03T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Interop performance debrief & A/B test targets

Sana — thanks again and for the logs. Quick confirmation and next steps from our side: 

Confirmed: 
- Redwood will avoid any infra rollouts during Wed 11/4–Thu 11/5 per your request.
- We'll run the replay and produce both server-side and client-observed p50/p95/p99. Rafael confirmed he can run the replay Tue night 11/3 and leave the cluster pinned for the window.

Deliverables and schedule: 
- Tue 11/3 EOD: initial replay results + per-token cost estimate (CSV + short one-pager).
- Wed 11/4–Thu 11/5: live A/B window (stable, no changes). We'll post rolling dashboards to the shared Drive folder linked below.
- Fri 11/6: consolidated AB report + recommended configuration and estimated monthly cost.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cRedwood/interop-plan
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/PEG-412

If that plan looks good I will lock the test window and send a calendar invite with the dashboard link.

Best — Dev
